commands.name: split
commands.description:
Split a .pptx file into individual single-slide files.

Examples:
  clippit pptx split deck.pptx --slides 1,3,6-9 --output slides
  clippit pptx split deck.pptx --output slides --manifest
  cat deck.pptx | clippit pptx split - --output slides --format json

options.name: --output
options.description: Output directory for the individual slide files (default: same directory as input, or the current directory when reading from stdin).

options.name: --slides
options.description: Slides to extract. Syntax: comma-separated list of 1-based slide numbers and/or inclusive ranges, e.g. '1,3,6-9'. Whitespace allowed around separators. Duplicates are deduplicated. Default: all slides.

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite existing output files. Without this flag the command fails on the first collision. [default: False]

options.name: --manifest
options.description: Also write a deck manifest (clippit pptx build run compatible) alongside the slides. Path: <outputDir>/<sourceBaseName>.manifest.json (or stdin.manifest.json for stdin input). Preserves source PPTX sections when present. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output format: json | text. Defaults to json when stdout is piped, text on a terminal. [default: Auto]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Suppress the success summary on stdout. Errors and exit codes are unaffected. [default: False]

arguments.name: INPUT
arguments.description: Path to the source .pptx file to split. Use '-' to read from stdin.

commands.name: build
commands.description:
Build a presentation from a manifest that assembles source .pptx files into sections.

Examples:
  clippit pptx build init --output deck.json
  clippit pptx build run deck.json --output final.pptx

commands.name: init
commands.description:
Scaffold a new empty deck manifest.

Examples:
  clippit pptx build init
  clippit pptx build init --output deck.json --force
  clippit pptx build init --output - > deck.json

options.name: --output
options.description: Path for the new manifest file (default: ./clippit-deck.json). Use '-' to write the manifest to stdout.

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite the manifest file if it already exists. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output format: json | text. Defaults to json when stdout is piped, text on a terminal. [default: Auto]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Suppress the success summary on stdout. Errors and exit codes are unaffected. [default: False]

commands.name: run
commands.description:
Build the final presentation from a deck manifest.

Examples:
  clippit pptx build run deck.json
  clippit pptx build run deck.json --output final.pptx --quiet
  cat deck.json | clippit pptx build run - --output - > final.pptx

options.name: --output
options.description: Override the output .pptx path from the manifest. Use '-' to write the binary to stdout.

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite the output presentation if it already exists. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output format: json | text. Defaults to json when stdout is piped, text on a terminal. [default: Auto]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Suppress the success summary on stdout. Errors and exit codes are unaffected. [default: False]

arguments.name: MANIFEST
arguments.description: Path to the deck manifest JSON file. Use '-' to read the manifest from stdin.

commands.name: verify
commands.description:
Validate that a .pptx file is a correct OpenXml presentation.

Examples:
  clippit pptx verify deck.pptx
  clippit pptx verify deck.pptx --format json
  clippit pptx verify deck.pptx --office-version Office2021
  cat deck.pptx | clippit pptx verify - --format json

options.description: OpenXml schema version to validate against: Office2007, Office2010, Office2013, Office2016, Office2019, Office2021, Microsoft365 (default: Microsoft365). [default: Microsoft365]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output format: json | text. Defaults to json when stdout is piped, text on a terminal. [default: Auto]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Suppress the success summary on stdout. Errors and exit codes are unaffected. [default: False]

arguments.name: INPUT
arguments.description: Path to the .pptx file to verify. Use '-' to read from stdin.

commands.name: verify

Examples:

  clippit word verify document.docx --format json
  clippit word verify document.docx --office-version Office2021
  cat document.docx | clippit word verify - --format json

options.description: OpenXml schema version to validate against: Office2007, Office2010, Office2013, Office2016, Office2019, Office2021, Microsoft365 (default: Microsoft365). [default: Microsoft365]

commands.name: to-html
commands.description:
Convert a .docx file to HTML/CSS.

Examples:
  clippit word to-html document.docx
  clippit word to-html document.docx --page-title "Q3 Report" --additional-css "body { max-width: 800px; }"
  clippit word to-html document.docx --inline-images --output -
  cat document.docx | clippit word to-html - --inline-images --format json

options.name: --output
options.description: Output path for the generated .html file. Defaults to <input>.html. Use '-' to write HTML content to stdout.

options.name: --page-title
options.description: HTML page <title>. Defaults to the source file name.

options.name: --additional-css
options.description: Extra CSS rules injected into the generated <style> block.

options.name: --css-prefix
options.description: Prefix for auto-generated CSS class names (default: pt-). [default: pt-]

options.name: --inline-images
options.description: Embed images as base64 data URIs instead of linking to external files. [default: False]

options.name: --no-fabricate-css
options.description: Skip CSS class generation and use inline style attributes instead. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output format: json | text. Defaults to json when stdout is piped, text on a terminal. [default: Auto]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Suppress the success summary on stdout. Errors and exit codes are unaffected. [default: False]

arguments.name: INPUT
arguments.description: Path to the .docx file to convert. Use '-' to read from stdin.

commands.name: from-html
commands.description:
Convert an HTML file to .docx.

Examples:
  clippit word from-html article.html
  clippit word from-html article.html -c styles.css -o article.docx
  clippit word from-html article.html --minor-font "Georgia" --font-size 11
  cat article.html | clippit word from-html - --base-uri https://example.com/images/ --format json

options.name: --output
options.description: Output path for the generated .docx file. Defaults to <input>.docx. Use '-' to write binary content to stdout.

options.name: --css
options.description: Path to an external author CSS file. When omitted, CSS is extracted from the HTML <style> element.

options.name: --default-css
options.description: Path to a default CSS file. When omitted, a built-in default CSS is used.

options.name: --user-css
options.description: Additional CSS rules to apply as user overrides.

options.name: --base-uri
options.description: Base URI for resolving relative image src references. Defaults to the source HTML file's parent directory.

options.name: --major-font
options.description: Theme major (heading) font name (default: Calibri Light).

options.name: --minor-font
options.description: Theme minor (body) font name (default: Times New Roman).

options.name: --font-size
options.description: Default font size in points (default: 12).

options.name: --format
options.description: Output format: json | text. Defaults to json when stdout is piped, text on a terminal. [default: Auto]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Suppress the success summary on stdout. Errors and exit codes are unaffected. [default: False]

arguments.name: INPUT
arguments.description: Path to the .html file to convert. Use '-' to read from stdin.

commands.name: to-html
commands.description:
Convert a spreadsheet range, sheet, or table to HTML/CSS.

Examples:
  clippit excel to-html spreadsheet.xlsx -o sheet.html
  clippit excel to-html spreadsheet.xlsx --sheet "Q3 Data" --range "B2:F15"
  clippit excel to-html spreadsheet.xlsx --table "SalesTable" -o - > table.html

options.name: --output
options.description: Output path for the generated .html file. Defaults to <input>.html. Use '-' to write HTML content to stdout.

options.name: --sheet
options.description: The sheet name to convert. Defaults to the first sheet found if neither --range nor --table are specified.

options.name: --range
options.description: Coordinates of the cell/range to convert (e.g. A1:D10). Requires --sheet option.

options.name: --table
options.description: Name of a defined Excel table to convert. Cannot be combined with --sheet or --range.

options.name: --page-title
options.description: HTML page <title>. Defaults to the source file name.

options.name: --additional-css
options.description: Extra CSS rules injected into the generated <style> block.

options.name: --css-prefix
options.description: Prefix for auto-generated CSS class names (default: pt-). [default: pt-]

options.name: --no-fabricate-css
options.description: Skip CSS class generation and use inline style attributes instead. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output format: json | text. Defaults to json when stdout is piped, text on a terminal. [default: Auto]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Suppress the success summary on stdout. Errors and exit codes are unaffected. [default: False]

arguments.name: INPUT
arguments.description: Path to the .xlsx file to convert. Use '-' to read from stdin.
